plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single sketch on an unlabeled coordinate plane showing a position vector broken into its horizontal and vertical parts. Two thin axes with arrowheads at all four ends meet at the origin; neither axis carries a name or numbers, though a few short tick marks are spaced along them. An orange arrow runs from the origin up and to the right into the first quadrant and is labeled v = ai + bj, with v, i, and j set in bold. A dark blue arrow extends from the origin along the horizontal axis to the point lying directly beneath the orange arrow's tip and is labeled ai below the axis. A second dark blue arrow rises vertically from that point to the tip of the orange arrow and is labeled bj. The two blue arrows and the orange one enclose a right triangle whose legs are the components and whose hypotenuse is the vector. Drawing the components as arrows joined head to tail makes the vector read as their sum rather than as an abstract pair. The sketch supports the magnitude of v being sqrt(a^2 + b^2), read straight off the legs of the triangle.

interactionPlan.concept: A position vector v = ai + bj is exactly the head-to-tail sum of its horizontal component ai and vertical component bj, and its length is the hypotenuse sqrt(a^2 + b^2) of the right triangle those components form.
elements: horizontal axis: thin black line with arrowheads at both ends and a few short tick marks, no numbers or name
vertical axis: thin black line with arrowheads at both ends and a few short tick marks, no numbers or name
origin where the two axes cross
orange vector arrow from the origin into the first quadrant, labeled in bold 'v = ai + bj' near its shaft
dark blue horizontal component arrow from the origin along the horizontal axis to the point beneath the vector tip, labeled 'ai' below the axis
dark blue vertical component arrow rising from the tip of ai up to the tip of v, labeled 'bj' to its right
right-angle marker at the corner where ai and bj meet (visible in magnitude view)
magnitude-view side labels: 'a' on the horizontal leg, 'b' on the vertical leg, and 'sqrt(a^2 + b^2)' on the orange hypotenuse
light shaded right-triangle interior in magnitude view

interactions.label: Horizontal component a
interactions.teaches: Changing a stretches or shrinks the horizontal leg ai and slides the vector's tip left/right, showing that the horizontal part of v is independent of the vertical part

interactions.label: Vertical component b
interactions.teaches: Changing b raises or lowers the vertical leg bj and the vector's tip, showing that the vertical part of v is independent of the horizontal part

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Switching to the magnitude triangle relabels the legs a and b and the hypotenuse sqrt(a^2 + b^2), revealing that the vector's length is just the Pythagorean theorem applied to its components

demo_steps.title: Vector as a sum of components
demo_steps.narration: The orange arrow v is drawn as the head-to-tail sum of the blue horizontal arrow ai and the blue vertical arrow bj — together they form a right triangle whose hypotenuse is v.

demo_steps.title: Move the components
demo_steps.narration: Drag a and b: the legs resize and the orange tip tracks the corner where they meet, so the vector visibly rebuilds itself from its two independent parts.

demo_steps.title: Read off the magnitude
demo_steps.narration: Toggle to the magnitude triangle: the legs are now lengths a and b and the hypotenuse is labeled sqrt(a^2 + b^2), so the vector's length follows directly from the Pythagorean theorem.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A vector is nothing more than its horizontal and vertical components joined head-to-tail, so its magnitude is the hypotenuse sqrt(a^2 + b^2) of the right triangle they enclose.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Unlabeled thin black axes crossing at the origin with double-ended arrowheads and a few evenly spaced tick marks. Orange vector arrow from origin into quadrant I (default tip near (3,2)) with bold label 'v = ai + bj' along its shaft. Dark blue horizontal arrow along the x-axis labeled 'ai' beneath it, and dark blue vertical arrow from that point up to the vector tip labeled 'bj'. In Components view show only these three arrows and labels. In Magnitude triangle view keep the same geometry but add a faint shaded right-triangle fill, a small right-angle square at the (a,0) corner, and relabel the legs 'a' and 'b' and the orange hypotenuse 'sqrt(a^2 + b^2)'. Cross-fade the label sets on toggle; keep arrowheads crisp and the orange clearly distinct from the dark blue.
